publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Microwave and RF Conference (IMaRC)
abstract: A novel Backward Wave Oscillator (BWO) suitable for work at millimeter Wave/THz regime, based on the Axial loaded Double Defected-Photonic Crystal (ADD-PC) Slow Wave Structure (SWS), is proposed. With the advantage of the excellent mode selectivity of the PC and the power handling capability of the metallic SWS, the ADD-PC is an ideal structure for Cherenkov radiation-based source/amplifier. The performance of the proposed BWO was investigated using a Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD)/Particle In Cell (PIC) simulation. The numerical simulation result shows a strong agreement with the theoretical expectations. A design example, generating a 200GHz electromagnetic wave at a 50mW level is presented.

articleTitle: A novel and compact ultra-wide band (UWB) filter using modified split ring resonator (MSRR)
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Microwave and RF Conference (IMaRC)
abstract: A novel and compact multi mode resonator (MMR) based ultra-wideband (UWB) (3.1 GHz-10.6 GHz) filter is proposed. Modified split ring resonator (MSRR) is used as multi-mode resonator (MMR) to achieve desired UWB pass band response by feeding thorough inter-digital coupled lines. Couple of shorted stubs is incorporated in order to improve sharp roll off at the pass band edges of the UWB pass band. Strongly coupled inter-digital coupled lines ensure low insertion loss in the pass band. Filter is fabricated on RT/Duroid 5880 substrate (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> =2.2 and h=0.785) with effective geometrical area 26 × 9 sq. mm. Excellent correlation between measured and simulated results ensures legitimacy of the device for UWB communications.

Author Keywords: Modified split ring resonator (MSRR) Multi Mode Resonator (MMR)
Inter-digital coupled line and Ultra Wide Band (UWB)

articleTitle: Cold measurement of a Ka-band Metal PBG waveguide
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Microwave and RF Conference (IMaRC)
abstract: In this article, we report the design and cold measurement of a Ka-band Metal Photonic Band Gap (MPBG) waveguide with a coupling from an external rectangular waveguide (WR-28) transition using a wraparound co-axial coupler. The metal PBG waveguide was realized by a triangular lattice of metal posts with a defect (removal of seven metal posts) at the center. The circular TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> travelling electromagnetic mode was supported by this defect portion without any mode competition. The circuit was fabricated and experimentally tested for its cold behavior. The circuit offered a wide band width of ~ 6 % of the centre frequency and this result has been close in agreement with simulations. This metal PBG waveguide circuit is suitable for gyro-TWT as an RF interaction circuit at microwave/millimeter wave higher harmonic operation.

articleTitle: Switchable reflector for dual-polarized antenna radar cross section reduction
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Microwave and RF Conference (IMaRC)
abstract: A switchable reflector which can switch reflection level using pin diodes for the vertical polarization and absorb for the horizontal polarization was proposed. The vertical polarized reflection coefficient was switched -29 dB with OFF-state diodes and -0.5 dB with ON-state diodes, and horizontal polarized one was less than -15 dB at 9 GHz. The reflector with ON-state diodes was applied to an antenna reflector of a dipole antenna and comparable radiation pattern to that with a metal reflector was obtained at 9 GHz. Therefore it can contribute to dual-polarized antenna RCS reduction at operating frequency without degrading antenna performance.

articleTitle: Design and development of triple band U Slot PIFA antenna
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Microwave and RF Conference (IMaRC)
abstract: In this paper triple band U shape Slot Planar Inverted F antenna (PIFA) design using three shorting post is presented. The antenna is designed to be integrated in portable devices. The linearly polarized antenna exhibits good impedance matching, Omni directional radiation pattern and relatively high gain. Frequency ratio of 1.27, 2.11 have been achieved. A prototype has been designed, fabricated and tested. Good agreement has been obtained between numerical simulations & experimental results.

articleTitle: In-orbit estimation of TT&C antenna coverage for satellite communication
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Microwave and RF Conference (IMaRC)
abstract: This paper presents the RF coverage analysis of TT&C antenna for MARS Orbiter Mission at S-band to predict the antenna performance during both transfer orbit phase as well as in-orbit phase (i.e. stowed and deployed configurations) taking into account the effect of the spacecraft structure and appendices like the solar array, déployable antenna and propellant tank. The main objective behind this analysis is for the decision making during the critical mission operations for commanding the satellite. This analysis is carried out by using the WIPL-D and MATLAB software. The predicted results of downlink TT&C antenna are compared with in-orbit measured data and found to have a good match.

articleTitle: Efficient finite element model order reduction of electromagnetic systems using fast converging Jacobi-Davidson Iteration
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Microwave and RF Conference (IMaRC)
abstract: Finite element models of electromagnetic scattering/radiation problems involve absorbing boundaries for the computational domain truncation. Model order reduction based on eigenspace projection for such systems, invariably, has to deal with nonlinear eigenvalue problems. For small systems, the eigenspaces can be extracted using linearization techniques. However, the linearized system is at least double in size compared to the original system. Therefore, selective extraction of interior eigenvalues can take prohibitively long using traditional shift-invert techniques. In this paper, a Jacobi-Davidson based algorithm is used to extract the desired part of the spectrum. The reduced system is setup quickly and is shown to be accurate within a desired frequency band.

articleTitle: PIM characterization at satellite level: An ISRO experience
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Microwave and RF Conference (IMaRC)
abstract: It is very essential to perform Passive Inter Modulation (PIM) measurement in multi-band communication satellites to avoid unwanted interference. Since source of PIM product can be any metallic or ferromagnetic objects, etc. it is very important to precisely identify the source of PEVI i.e from external environment or satellite transponder chain. For this reason, before conducting any PEVI measurement at satellite level in any anechoic chamber it is usual practice to measure the inherent PIM level of the chamber at measured frequencies. In this paper, procedure for PEVI characterization at satellite level is discussed. Also, one case study is discussed when, PIM product was observed in one satellite, the sequence of operations that were carried out to precisely identify the source of PEVI and corrective action that was taken to suppress them.

articleTitle: Location and origin of traps in InGaP-GaAs by GR noise measurement and simulation
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Microwave and RF Conference (IMaRC)
abstract: A thorough approach to the location and origin of traps generated in InGaP/GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT) by low frequency noise characterization and reliable physics-based simulation is discussed. Physics-based simulation together with the low frequency equivalent short-circuit current noise sources (Sib, Sic) experimental results reveal an electron trap located at the 5-InGaP/GaAs heterointerface and at the InGaP/nitride interface. For the first time, power spectral density (PSD) curves of (Sib, Sic) in the 100 Hz to 1 MHz frequency range for current densities up to 20 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> are demonstrated and are in agreement with those obtained from physics-based simulation.
